title: Cell Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll zoom into a cell — the smallest unit of life.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology Cell Biology walkthrough — animal vs plant cells, prokaryotes vs eukaryotes, and the size units used to measure them.

concepts.def: The smallest functional unit of a living organism
Cell control centre — holds the DNA
Site of aerobic respiration — release energy
Cellulose layer giving plant cells their shape
Cell without a true nucleus (e.g. bacteria)

walkthroughs.body_html:
A cell is the smallest unit that's alive.

Some organisms are just one cell. You are made of trillions.

Cells have parts called organelles — tiny machines doing different jobs.

Both have a nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, ribosomes, and mitochondria.

Plants also have:

- A cell wall (cellulose) for support
- Chloroplasts for photosynthesis
- A permanent vacuole full of cell sap

Prokaryotes (like bacteria) have no nucleus. Their DNA floats in the cytoplasm as a single loop, plus small extra rings called plasmids.

Cells are tiny. Useful units:

- 1 mm = 1000 µm (micrometres)
- 1 µm = 1000 nm (nanometres)

A typical animal cell is about 20 µm wide.

options: Nucleus
Mitochondria

Cell membrane

mcqs.q: What is the main role of mitochondria?
options: Photosynthesis
Aerobic respiration
Protein synthesis
DNA storage

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.
Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.

mcqs.q: What is the main role of mitochondria in a cell?
options: Mitochondria store sunlight and release it for photosynthesis.
Mitochondria produce energy by creating it from nothing.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
To carry out aerobic respiration, producing ATP that cells use as an energy currency.
Yes — plants respire all the time to release energy; they also photosynthesise when there is light.
Plants only photosynthesise and do not respire; respiration is for animals only.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
